rationale:
The reviewed tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. I judged this from the supplied test source only and did not request any implementation source.

- **Resolving a selector from the root against the retained outline**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It asserts the text equals the item's span and the `structural_hash` matches.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` selects percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates and anonymous `block@hash` and `section@hash` items.
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects `#1` and `#2` duplicates and nested paths.
  - `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects line items and checks their text.
  - The empty selector is checked in `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` and `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`.
- **Owned result that shares the snapshot and fingerprinting rules**
  - `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` in the markdown test and `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())` in the Rust test show the outline is shared.
  - `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` shows the fingerprint scheme survives selection, including after the language and scheme are dropped. A different scheme gives a different fingerprint.
- **No extra file read, and usable after the original handle is dropped**
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` drops `file` and rewrites the file on disk.
  - It then asserts that the selected contents keep their text and fingerprint, and that `selected.select("")` still returns the original full text.
  - `from_id` fails after the edit, which confirms the file really changed.
- **`id()` and `text()` semantics**
  - The test above asserts `selected_again.id()` equals the requested id and `retained_root.id()` equals the root id.
  - The Rust test asserts `text()` includes the attached doc comment and attributes.
  - The redaction test asserts `selected.text()` still contains the raw token while `format()` redacts it.
- **Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable**
  - `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` selects the duplicated `alpha` line by its shared selector.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` selects the duplicated `same` lines successfully.
- **Invalid, missing and ambiguous selections return errors**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` covers the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing item `fn[absent]`.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` covers ambiguity. Duplicate non-`line` kinds return an error containing "ambiguous". A `line` kind whose hashes differ also errors.
  - The CSS test asserts that an un-numbered `rule[a%20b]` is an error.

I found no obligation of the subject that lacks a test with a relevant assertion. The remaining selector-grammar detail belongs to the cited `selector_syntax` requirement and is not reassessed here.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineId;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
